correctness.rationale: All finite n>=3, 0<p<1: relative Fourier kernel solves the killed Poisson equation; discrete Poisson kernel summation, exact strict convexity, odd/even endpoint analysis, uniform differentiable exponential correction, and Wald count identity verify the entire theorem. originality.rationale: The core Markovian cycle rendezvous reduction, finite examples and convexity are earlier findings (Alpern 1995; Alpern–Gal 2003). Zhang et al. 2014 cover random-start Fourier means. Current accepted increment is the adjacent-start all-n asymptotic clock optimizer with sharp n inverse correction, and the conflicting move-count optimum. Real published-finding corpus queries and accessible primary texts found no implication of this increment; strongest inaccessible 1995 article explicitly remains a material historical-priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The two natural objective functions for adjacent-start encounter, elapsed ticks and actual individual moves, have incompatible optimum rates. Quantifying the p_n two-thirds limit and its size correction is a nontrivial natural design invariant; linear rather than quadratic scale at one-step initial displacement makes the distinction concrete and potentially useful in collision/mobility tradeoffs. Not claimed as a general-graph or general-rendezvous breakthrough.
